narrative.overview: The portfolio is one working paper solar system, not a dark starfield with cards floating on it. A large-format 1970s science annual is the physical reference: warm stock, flat process inks, a real gutter, die-cut discs, fold-out dossiers, and a pull tab that sets the system moving. The paper is the page; the solar system is the navigation. The interface is an Experience surface, so the artifact leads. A visitor reads the masthead on the left page, sees four named worlds on the plate, pulls the tab, and unfolds a dossier with real work, skills, and contact details. The flat guide below is the printable, machine-readable edition. The tone is playful, tactile, and quietly confident; it never becomes a children's book or a sci-fi console.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream stock and prussian ink; the deep desk is the only dark field.
Five flat spot inks: cobalt, tomato, sunflower, forest, and lilac.
Square paper sheets, hairline orbits, die-cut circles, and fold-out panels.
Self-hosted Young Serif for the display; Archivo for body and labels.
Search, hover, focus, touch, reduced motion, no-JS, and print are all designed states.
One authored motion: the orbit; the map steadies on hover/focus and starts paused on touch.

rules.name: The Paper Ground Rule
rules.body: Every screen is a sheet of warm stock. The deep desk exists to hold the book, not to become a second page.

rules.name: The Spot-Ink Rule
rules.body: Cobalt, tomato, sunflower, forest, and lilac are flat printing inks. Each world owns one; never gradient them, never glow them, and never scatter all five as UI chrome.

rules.name: The Registration Rule
rules.body: Keep the print marks: the 1px off-register tomato offset on display headings and the registration target at the plate's top-left. They are evidence of the press, not decoration.

rules.name: The One Display Voice Rule
rules.body: Young Serif is the only display face. No second serif, no system display face, no condensed substitute.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A label never sits above a heading. The heading carries its own weight; labels live beside, below, or in the margin.

rules.name: The Paper-Edge Rule
rules.body: A shadow describes a physical layer: it carries an offset and a blur. If it reads as a halo, remove it.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Rule
rules.body: Circles are objects punched out of the page, never badges added to it. They carry no gloss, no border radius beyond 50%, and no gradient sphere shading.

dos: Do keep the warm stock, prussian ink, five flat spot inks, and the grain.
Do keep the gutter, the 0px paper edges, the die-cut discs, the registration target, and the 1px ink misregistration.
Do keep the plate key; the worlds must be named above the fold at 390, 768, and 1440.
Do keep the four project moons visible at rest and the Work dossier's moon rows.
Do keep the paper pull tab at every width, including its die-cut hole and active deep-tomato state.
Do keep the 32px controls, 2px focus ring, keyboard trap, reduced-motion pause, touch pause, and flat-guide fallback.
Do keep the print stylesheet: white paper, flat guide only, project URLs.
donts: Don't introduce glass, backdrop blur, neon, gradient text, a dark starfield, or a glowing-gradient planet.
Don't turn the spread into same-size cards, pill chips, or a dashboard.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't gradient the spot inks or use them as generic UI chrome.
Don't hide the world names, the moons, or the pull tab on small screens.
Don't shrink the desktop spread into a phone; the phone is a single page, not a miniature book.
Don't invent clients, metrics, testimonials, a CV, or a live AI chat; use only the real portfolio content.
Don't use a system display face, Unicode glyph icons, or a second display serif.
Don't remove the flat guide, the print edition, or the no-JS anchors.
